text.p: Pamida Holdings Corp said Monday it received approval for certain actions that will allow the mass merchandise retailer to recapitalize.

Pamida said two preconditions to the company's previously announced proposal for payment of its outstanding promissory notes with common stock and reclassification of its outstanding preferred stock into common stock, were satisfied.

The reclassification of the preferred stock requires the approval of both the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of preferred stock and the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of common stock. Pamida said it now has obtained the required preferred stockholder approval.

In addition, Pamida said that Alex. Brown & Sons Inc considers fair the proposed note and preferred stock transactions to the holders of the presently outstanding common stock of the company. This opinion was required for completion of the proposed transactions.

The only remaining precondition to completion of the transactions is approval by the company's present common stockholders. Pamida has filed preliminary proxy material with the Securities and Exchange Commission relating to a special meeting of common stockholders to vote on the various elements of the proposed transactions.
A meeting date will be set upon completion of the SEC review of the proxy material.

"Completion of these transactions will improve Pamida's common stock capitalization by over $35 million and eliminates a substantial earnings drain from our income statement," said Steven Fishman, chairman and chief executive officer of Pamida. "This represents a very positive step in our efforts to improve the company's capital structure and to enhance our competitiveness in executing our small town niche market strategy," he added.
